entries.title: Sixth beluga whale rescued from Canada dies in San Diego, following four deaths at the Shedd
entries.summary: <p>Another beluga whale rescued from the shuttered Marineland aquarium in Ontario, Canada, has died, SeaWorld in San Diego announced.</p><p>Cyprus, a 9-year-old beluga, stopped eating this weekend and declined quickly, said a Facebook post from the aquarium. He was initially doing well since arriving in San Diego in August, but belugas, like many species, can hide their discomfort or face underlying health concerns, the facility said.</p><p>That brings the total number of Marineland whales to die since being rescued to six, including four at Chicago's Shedd Aquarium and one at Oceanografic Valencia in Spain.</p><p>At the Shedd, the most recent death was Caspian, a 27-year-old female, that died Oct. 7. Peekachu, a 23-year-old female, died Aug. 25, and Rain, a 20-year-old female, died Sept. 2. Osiris, a 26-year-old female, died Sept. 21. The rescued beluga in Spain, Jelly Bean, died Sept. 18.</p><p>A resident beluga at the Shedd, Beethoven, also died recently at 34, likely due to age-related issues, the aquarium said.</p><p>Marineland closed this summer after facing financial ruin and loud criticism from animal rights activists, some of whom have also questioned the safety of transferring the whales to other aquariums.</p><p>The SeaWorld post said, "Like our colleagues at the other AZA-accredited facilities that rescued these belugas, we understood each animal would be navigating a significant transition and that their complete health picture, including conditions that may have developed over time, could only become clearer through ongoing assessment and care."</p><p>SeaWorld is still working to acclimate the rest of the belugas from Marineland, and staff acknowledged it would take time for the animals to adjust.</p><p>"The other rescued belugas in our care continue to be in stable health and remain under close monitoring as they continue to adjust to their surroundings," the aquarium said. "As we have indicated, this process will take a considerable amount of time. Our commitment to the health, well-being and care of these belugas, like every animal we rescue, continues." </p>
entries.author: Mary Norkol

entries.title: Analyzing Game 1 of the WNBA Finals
entries.summary: <p>SAN FRANCISCO — You’re probably feeling pretty annoyed right now if you’re the Dream, <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/wnba/2026/10/17/valkyries-fans-meet-coach-natalie-nakases-expectations-in-game-1-of-the-wnba-finals" >having lost a Game 1</a> in which you led for 75% of it, and had the Valkyries offense looking like a fish flopping on land.</p><p>In fact, the half-court offense appeared so halting and uncertain about where any openings were that I had to ask a couple of Bay Area journalists after the game what the Valkyries’ strategy on offense even is.</p><p>They said it was waiting for the Dream to make a mistake.</p><p>The problem with that is that the Dream don’t make very many. They’re long, quick, and in each other’s gaps. As a result, so many Valkyries possessions ended in a desperation heave, or a forced drive into Dream defenders that hadn’t been shifted.</p><p>The Dream enjoyed a lead for much of the third quarter until a Valkyries run — which included a Kiah Stokes tip-in, an unlikely roll on a Kaila Charles’ three-point shot, and a breakdown from the Dream leaving Charles wide open for a layup — gave them the lead.</p><p>Even through his normal stoicism, you could tell Dream coach Karl Smesko was very attuned to how luck and tiny mistakes swung the game in the Valkyries favor.</p><p>“I thought our team defended excellent, but when a game is this close even a couple breakdowns can make the difference,” Smesko said.</p><p>The problem that Smesko likely spent Sunday mulling over is that the Dream’s half-court offense was really no better than the Valkyries’. Though I’m no expert on the the Dream either, I can tell you that the one thing every half-court offense is supposed to do — swing the ball from one side of the court to the other — did not happen. Like the Valkyries, it was a lot of one pass then fire away.</p><p>“We had a couple of dry spells where we just weren’t working together as well as you need to against this [Valkyries] defense,” Smesko said.</p><p>They also turned their back on what had been working from the jump. Forward Angel Reese built them a lead in the first quarter, then only touched the ball in scoring position twice in the second half.</p><p>“Maybe that was just on me,” Reese said. “I wasn’t aggressive enough with the ball and trying to get the ball and to get to spots.<br>So definitely going to do a better job of that next game.”</p><p>Smesko also took responsibility, saying they need to do a better job getting the ball to Reese.</p><p>The bright side is that “giving Reese the ball” and actually moving the ball from side to side don’t really seem that difficult to correct heading into Game 2. The other bright side is that despite Dream superstar Rhyne Howard finishing with a measly 12 points, they still only lost by four. They also had two wide-open shots at the end that could have won the game.</p><p>“Naz [Hillmon] had a good look at three,” Smesko said. “Rhyne had a good look at three. We knock down either of those we’re not talking about whatever mistakes we made.</p><p>“But that’s what this game comes down to. You have two shots go in and out. At some point in the game, they bank in a three. We were right there. So that’s why it hurts a little bit. But it also motivates us. We know we’re capable of doing.”</p><p>This WNBA Finals represents a changing of the guard. The Valkyries and Dream knocked off the Aces and the Liberty, super-teams that have dominated the last five years, and they reached the pinnacle in large part by feasting on other teams’ mistakes.</p><p>Which is why Game 1 felt like such a staring contest; there just aren’t very many mistakes left to be mined.</p>

entries.title: Evanston, New Trier investigate reports of racist, homophobic slurs during football game at new Ryan Field
entries.summary: <p>Two suburban school districts are investigating after reports of homophobic and racist slurs at Friday night's football game between the two schools. Played at Northwestern University's newly opened Ryan Field, the game was supposed to be a season highlight for New Trier and Evanston Township high schools. More than 25,000 fans attended, according to some reports.</p><p>New Trier fans directed racist and homophobic comments toward members of the Evanston marching band, according to a joint statement from both districts' superintendents.</p><p>"Friday evening should have been an opportunity to celebrate our students, spirited competition, and the longstanding traditions of our two school communities," the statement said. "For the ETHS Marching Band, it was an especially meaningful opportunity to do what they love: share their talents and proudly represent their school. No student should leave an event where they came to perform, compete, or support their peers feeling that their dignity or belonging were demeaned."</p><p>Administrators at both districts are working together to investigate the reports and encourage anyone with information about the incident to contact their school's administration.</p>

entries.title: Bears beat Falcons 31-23 in QB Caleb Williams' return
entries.summary: <p>ATLANTA — <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a> quarterback Caleb Williams stepped up in the pocket, shuffled right and started sprinting toward the sideline. He looked downfield until he locked eyes with his biggest target, then threw across his body toward tight end Colston Loveland, who was sandwiched between two Falcons defenders at the goal line.</p><p>Loveland caught the ball as he was smacked by the two players for the first touchdown of the Bears’ 31-23 victory Sunday against the Falcons. Williams soon delivered another hit — a gentle head bump — before taking off his helmet and celebrating on the sideline.</p><p>‘‘Just let it rip,’’ Williams said. ‘‘Let the emotions rip.’’</p><p>It was a show of emotion a month in the making, ever since Williams suffered a torn right hamstring in the fourth quarter of a Week 2 loss against the Vikings. And it was a spark the Bears desperately needed in the wake of a 31-7 thrashing at the hands of the Packers a week ago.</p><p>Williams’ performance was much more than a ball of emotion, however. He was a stone-cold assassin, completing 30 of 36 passes for 305 yards and a 111.2 passer rating. He completed his first 12 passes, including a third-down hook-and-ladder to wide receiver Rome Odunze, who shoveled the ball to running back Roschon Johnson. It set up the touchdown to Loveland, who finished with a season-high 65 yards on six catches.</p><p>In a clean pocket, Williams went 24-for-24 for 248 yards, according to NFL Next Gen Stats. No NFL quarterback has completed that many passes without an incompletion since at least 2018.</p><p>‘‘Let the emotions fly,’’ Williams said. ‘‘But when it’s time to be in control, when it’s time to lock in and look the guys in the eyes, they want to feel your control over yourself, your control of the huddle. And then from there we can go out there and execute.’’</p><p>It was one of the best performances of Williams’ career. Given the stakes, it might have been the most important. The Bears were at a ‘‘crossroads,’’ coach Ben Johnson said, after losing to the Packers. Williams reset their direction. His teammates felt it.</p><p>‘‘He has the juice,’’ Odunze said.</p><p>As an added bonus, Williams said his hamstring wasn’t sore after the game, though he’ll need to continue treatment for it through the rest of the season. Williams ran four times for three yards, including a two-yard sneak for a first down with 2:46 lefty. That was far different than his last complete game, when he ran 10 times for 65 yards in Week 1.</p><p>This was the dream scenario the Bears had in mind when they decided to start Williams a week after Tyson Bagent struggled against the Packers. The plan started with a brief meeting in Johnson’s office early last week.</p><p>‘‘I walked in his office, dapped him up and said, ‘Let’s get this going this week,’ ’’ Williams said. ‘‘And I walked out after that.’’</p><p>The energy from Williams’ return crackled through the stadium. The Bears led 14-0 at the end of the first quarter and never trailed. There were so many Bears fans inside Mercedes-Benz Stadium that the Falcons practiced all week with crowd noise and used a silent count on offense. The crowd erupted with every Williams success.</p><p>The Bears’ defense felt the energy, too, giving up seven points through the first three quarters. The Falcons rallied for 16 points in the fourth and marched for a touchdown against Bears backups before Johnson put the starters back in. The Bears were trying to lighten the defensive workload with a game Thursday against the Patriots, Johnson said, but reversed course to lock down the victory.</p><p>The Bears’ special-teamers got in on the act, too, recovering a fumbled kickoff and a muffed punt — the latter on Tory Taylor’s curving ‘‘banana ball’’ — that contributed to 10 points.</p><p>‘‘The fact that we started fast, really in all three phases, was huge for us, as well as something that we had also talked about the night before,’’ Johnson said. ‘‘If you could write a script, that’s what we would want to do against a team like this. We’ve got to come out of the gate hot.’’</p><p>Earlier in the week, it was Williams who was hot. He used his first news conference since Sept. 23 to rail against what he said were erroneous reports about the severity of his injury. What went unspoken was his<br>annoyance with those who mocked him leaving the game against the Vikings emotional and on a golf cart.</p><p>Williams made no mention of that beef after the game. But as he jogged to the locker room after the victory, he looked at the assembled media and, with a smile, paraphrased an old Kirk Cousins line.</p><p>‘‘Y’all like that?’’ he said.</p><p>The answer from the teammates waiting for him in the locker room — and from fans at home and in the stadium — was a resounding yes.</p><p>When Williams entered the locker room, he got a game ball. He told his teammates how hard it was to fight through the injury.</p><p>‘‘It was just me having a consistent positive mindset throughout the weeks over myself — and about myself — of being able to get back, trying to get back, fighting to get back,’’ Williams said. ‘‘And when I get back, just to show them who I am. And who we are.’’</p><div class="RelatedList Enhancement" data-module data-align-center> <div class="RelatedList-title">Related</div> <ul class="RelatedList-items"> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/10/18/bears-falcons-grades-caleb-williams-kyler-gordon-colston-loveland-chicago-atlanta-nfl" >Bears’ grades are in. How did they do against the Falcons?</a> </li> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/10/18/bears-ben-johnson-was-back-in-his-bag-in-crossroads-win-against-falcons" >Bears’ Ben Johnson was back in his bag in ‘crossroads’ win against Falcons</a> </li> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/10/18/bears-cb-kyler-gordon-goes-off-with-3-sacks-in-return-from-injury-everything-i-wanted" >Bears CB Kyler Gordon gets 3 sacks in return from injury in 31-23 win vs. Falcons: ‘Everything I wanted’</a> </li> </ul> </div> <p></p>

You will work diligently to achieve what you want to do. However, social plans might suddenly change. Parents should know this could be an accident-prone day for your kids, so be vigilant.</p><h2>Pisces (Feb. 19-March 20)</h2><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="HtmlModule"><a class="AnchorLink" id="html-embed-module-4d0000" name="html-embed-module-4d0000"></a><div class="HoroscopeStarbox HoroscopeStarbox_five"> <div class="HoroscopeStarbox_container"> <svg class="HoroscopeStar"><use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use></svg> <svg class="HoroscopeStar"><use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use></svg> <svg class="HoroscopeStar"><use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use></svg> </div> <div class="HoroscopeStarbox_description"> <p>An <b>average</b> day</p> </div> </div> <style> .HoroscopeStarbox { background: #f8f8f8; display: flex; align-items: center; } .HoroscopeStarbox_container { display: grid; grid-gap: 5px; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr 1fr 1fr 1fr; padding: 20px; width: 40%; min-width: 160px; max-width: 200px; } .HoroscopeStarbox_description { padding: 20px; font-family: var(--font-1); font-size: var(--body-2); } .HoroscopeStarbox_container svg { object-fit: cover; aspect-ratio: 1 / 1; width: 100%; } </style> </div> </div><p>This is a restless day for you. Even a romantic interest with someone afar or from another culture? (Most curious.)</p><h2>If today is your birthday</h2><p>Actor Michael Gambon (1940-2023) shares your birthday. You're independent, free-spirited and complex. You appreciate beauty in simple things. You're a fearless peace lover. This year, your creativity, zest and desire for life are at a pinnacle! Nurture the happiness and beauty you have within. Let your guard down, and loosen up a bit. Have fun, but remember your goals.</p>
